newsitem.title: CHILE: Chilean shares end losing streak, close firm.
newsitem.headline: Chilean shares end losing streak, close firm.

text.p: Capping a four session losing run, Chilean blue chips ended sharply higher on strong foreign demand as fears over a possible devaluation in Brazil subsided, said dealers.
The positive trend is seen continuing for the rest of the week, they said.
"Wednesday's rally was a technical rebound which is likely to be maintained for the rest of the week, although in a more moderate pace," said one broker.
The 40-share closed up 1.06 percent at 132.65 points.
The all-share index firmed 0.51 percent to 5,745.9 points amid turnover of 10.8 billion pesos.

Chilean stocks took their cue from the recovery in the regional bourses, led by the Brazilian Bovespa index which charged up nearly nine percent at the close. The surge allowed Sao Paulo stocks to regain all ground lost in Tuesday's slide.

"A gentle wave of foreign buy orders from clear from the morning and the recovery of regional bolsas also inspired local investors, said one dealer. Winners included winery San Pedro, which rallied on news of strong sales growth in the first half of the year, said traders.
San Pedro, one of Chile's largest wineries, ended up 4.52 percent at 3.7 pesos.
Other gainers included drug-maker LabChile, up 3.67 percent at 565 pesos and supermarket chain D&S, which rose 3.88 percent to 509 pesos.
Losers included glass producer Cristales, down 1.45 percent at 3,400 pesos and Banco Santander which shed 1.03 percent at 28-2/3 pesos.
